notes.text: The literal condition “Pour tout $x\in L$” is stronger than the support condition used by the proof, and beta literally has $x\in\mathscr L$, not $x\in|\mathscr L|$. Taking $L=\{a,b\}$ and $F=\{\{a\}\}$ refutes equivalence with condition 1 as written; P00–P01 prove the theorem on the support, without changing either frozen expression.
notes.context: Differs from the normalized proposition in S5 §1 / SA21-R5-01; E119/27–30 gives the stratification programme but no such support lemma.

notes.text: The frozen boundary has plain $B\subset A$, as does the union in alpha, and no extra strictness stroke or inequality was adopted from S. The boundary must exclude $B=A$, while alpha at $A=B$ and the marginal delta-prime require weak inclusion, so one global strict interpretation cannot serve every occurrence. The mathematical convention in P00 is explicit and is not an emendation of the ink.
notes.context: Contradicts the proposed strict ink reading of SA21-K5-04 while retaining its mathematical warning; E119/31–34 has no corresponding formula.

notes.place: margin referring to GF VIII, page 37
notes.text: “variante ‘indexée’ formellement plus forte” is an explicit forward lead: an indexed family could distinguish coincident subsets, whereas the present family is a set of subsets. That distinction should be tested before identifying these figures with categories carrying automorphisms or repeated strata; the cited GF VIII page is outside the supplied scans and is not checked here.
notes.context: Adds a precise indexing warning to E119/37, where the stratum index set is replaced by an essentially finite category, and to E119/59 on internal categories.

notes.text: The step “A minimal” implies “un plus petit élément” is justified by alpha, which produces a member through the point inside every intersection. P01 checks this implication directly: minimality forces that member to equal $A$, so no unjustified uniqueness-of-minimal-element argument is needed.
notes.context: Restates, with the needed hypothesis exposed, S5 §1 / SA21-R5-01; no matching proof occurs in E119/27–41.

notes.text: The proof begins “On suppose gamma et delta” but ends “Par eta”, so eta is used despite its omission in the opening list. This is harmless for the intended three-condition proposition, but the two-condition statement alone is false in the infinite case of N004-3.
notes.context: Differs from the silently completed hypothesis list in S5 §1; E119/34 likewise discusses provisional axioms, without settling this set-theoretic implication.

notes.place: proof together with scan002 marginal delta-prime
notes.text: The marginal replacement of “delta, eta” by delta-prime really works on the support: a decomposition of every closed member into the strata below it, together with uniqueness of the stratum through a point, gives the least-member property. P01 supplies the missing separate proof and makes the weak inclusion in that decomposition explicit.
notes.context: Adds an explicit proof to the margin and restates the normalized alternative checked by S5 §1; E119/36 supplies a more geometric decomposition problem rather than this lemma.

notes.text: “beta … automatique” for an artinian family follows by choosing a minimal member through a point; the descending-chain counterexample with nonempty intersection shows why the hypothesis matters. P02 also proves the stronger useful fact that gamma alone implies eta for an artinian family, explaining the failure of the finite draft below.
notes.context: Restates S5 §1 / SA21-R5-02 and SA21-R5-03 with a written proof; E119/39 emphasizes finiteness of stratifications but contains no artinian version.

notes.place: cancelled examples and slanted correction; both on scan004
notes.text: “Exemple idiot” explicitly withdraws the drawn finite counterexample and points instead to “I infini”, GF VIII pages 44–45. The claim that eta is not redundant is not withdrawn, but these finite drawings cannot establish it; the cited later example remains outside this return.
notes.context: Restates the withdrawal recorded by SA21-K5-05 and S5 §1, now with the independently read deletion state; E119/34 offers only a general comparison with tentative axioms.

notes.text: Our explicit test-family takes $A=\{p,a\}$, $B_n=\{p\}\cup\{b_m:m\ge n\}$, and includes $A$, $\{a\}$, all $B_n$, and all $\{b_n\}$. Its nonempty strata are singletons, so gamma and delta hold, while $A^\circ=\{p\}\subset B_0$ and $A\not\subset B_0$ refute eta. P02 gives the calculation; no identity with Grothendieck’s unavailable GF VIII example, and no novelty, is claimed.
notes.context: Adds a concrete infinite witness to the lead in S5 §1; E119/27–41 and RS do not provide this example.
notes.confidence: High: every boundary and stratum is calculated explicitly; the descending chain is visible.

notes.place: surjection to an ordered set and topology
notes.text: “Se donner … une famille admissible … revient” to a poset $I$, support $S$, and surjection $S\to I$ is the exact reconstruction $A_i=p^{-1}(\downarrow i)$ proved in P03. Here downsets are **closed**, whereas STRATA 0.1 uses downset **opens**, so comparison with that register must replace $I$ by $I^{op}$. The manuscript gives the elementary data model, not a new proof of the register’s exit or coefficient theorems.
notes.context: Adds an explicit set-theoretic presentation to E119/36–37 and differs in orientation from RS STRATA 0.1 / WG2 B15 (§1.2).

notes.text: The uncertain “un ens. fini|fin.” of additional closed subsets cannot be a general finiteness requirement. All singletons of $\mathbb N$ together with all initial segments $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ for $n\ge1$ form a preadmissible family with infinitely many members having empty stratum; P03 describes the additions as arbitrary nonprincipal downsets.
notes.context: Adds a counter-test to the margin, not treated in S5’s summary; E119/39’s finite filtration does not impose finiteness on this abstract definition.

notes.text: The unqualified identification of the members with “parties fermées irréd.” needs complete join-irreducibility, or a finite poset. For the chain $\mathbb N$ with closed downsets, the whole space is irreducible in the ordinary finite-union sense but has no greatest point, so it is not a principal closed set. Scan012’s “au sens fort” supplies the distinction required by P03.
notes.context: Qualifies the unqualified assertion in S5 §1 and connects the two manuscript margins; E119/36 has ordered indices but no irreducibility theorem.

notes.text: The margin “un préordre sur S” separates point-level equivalence from order on the quotient: the quotient is an actual poset because distinct members are distinct subsets. This is a concrete positive model for the intake’s quotient-preorder question, but does not establish that an arbitrary partition into locally closed pieces has the same property.
notes.context: Adds a sufficient construction to RS INTAKE 20261114 §13.4 (cote150 scan003) and differs from the extra geometric structures of E119/36.

notes.text: The criterion “i≤j≤k, i,k∈J ⇒ j∈J” is precisely order convexity. P04 proves both directions without a finiteness assumption using $J=(\uparrow J)\cap(\downarrow J)$; this identifies locally closed saturated subsets in the topology of scan005.
notes.context: Adds an elementary order-theoretic criterion to E119/39’s locally closed strata and to the question in RS INTAKE 20261114 §13.4.

notes.place: Boolean algebra NB and inserted finiteness
notes.text: The insertion “si … fini” is essential to the claim that the generated Boolean algebra consists of all saturated subsets. For the singleton figure on $\mathbb N$, the ordinary Boolean algebra generated using finite operations is finite–cofinite, whereas every subset is saturated. P04 therefore checks the finite claim, not its unrestricted extension.
notes.context: Restates S5 §1’s finite qualification and differs from any reading that imports arbitrary unions into Boolean generation; E119/39 uses finite families in its geometric dévissage.

notes.text: The words “modérées ou … constructibles” here name saturation relative to a finite figure, without choosing a geometric tame category. They provide a finite Boolean vocabulary for the programme, but do not prove triangulability, tubular existence, or comparison of tame theories.
notes.context: Adds a combinatorial special case to E119/31–35 and differs in scope from RS MPL_150_044-084 Q9 and the planning bridge WG2 B15 (§1.2).

notes.text: The definition “qui est fermé dans” the family means down-closed for inclusion, not merely a subfamily which happens to be admissible. P05 verifies that all proper lower members, hence each boundary and open stratum, remain unchanged; this is the invariant used repeatedly in later union and refinement arguments.
notes.context: Restates S5 §1 / SA21-R5-05 and gives the set-level closed-part analogue of E119/28–30’s closed-pair decomposition.

notes.text: The converse uses the induced equivalence classes and the inserted saturation of the smaller support. P05 checks that the support is already saturated because the smaller family consists of ambient members, so the insertion makes an available fact explicit rather than adding an independent hypothesis; the remaining argument forces every ambient lower member into the subfamily.
notes.context: Restates the complete criterion in S5 §1 and adds precision to the order/partition comparison relevant to RS INTAKE 20261114 §13.4; E119/36 supplies only the broader stratification setting.

notes.text: The parenthesis “Psi adm.” is not the hypothesis that gives $B^\circ\ne\varnothing$, since $B$ is initially a member of the ambient family. The intended proof uses admissibility of that ambient family; P05 explains why equality of the induced strata then identifies the closed members, without replacing the frozen parenthesis.
notes.context: Qualifies the clean proof summary of S5 §1 / SA21-R5-05; E119/27–41 has no corresponding parenthesis.

notes.place: compatibility proposition, a / a-prime / b / c
notes.text: “deux sous-familles adm. d’une famille adm.” is equivalent to the union being admissible with both families closed in it; agreement on the common support is a stronger condition than merely agreeing on its partition. P05 checks the least-member gluing argument, and the stratum-by-stratum version added on scan012 gives a local recognition test.
notes.context: Restates S5 §2 / SA21-R5-06 and adds a set-theoretic compatibility test to E119/28–30’s gluing language; it does not replace E’s attachment maps.

notes.text: “Reste à prouver b⇒c, c⇒a” marks temporary proof obligations, not a standing conjecture. The first begins immediately and the continuation runs through scans009–010; P05 records the completed mathematical argument.
notes.context: Restates C01’s standing item and S5 §2, while E119/35’s still-unclear tubular uniqueness is a genuinely different unresolved issue.

notes.place: remaining union condition, continued on scan010
notes.text: “Il reste à prouver que si …” concerns the lower-member condition needed for the union, and the page ends mid-sentence at “les B en”. Its continuation supplies the missing cases on scan010, so the break is physical pagination rather than abandonment of the proof.
notes.context: Restates C01’s standing item and S5 §2 / SA21-R5-06; the context E119/28–30 does not give this particular compatibility proof.

notes.text: The proof’s common-lower-member condition shows exactly what set-level “recollement” remembers: the same subsets with the same least members on the overlap. It supplies no maps from links or normal fibres, so it cannot by itself furnish the coherent gluing data in the earlier geometric programme.
notes.context: Differs in retained data from E119/36 and119/58–59; bears on the scope of RS STRATA C.8 and EXIT_ONE_TYPE P1d1, whose full statements are carried as background.

notes.text: “cette dernière condition ne suffit nullement” is demonstrated already by $F=\{\{a\},\{a,b\}\}$ and $G=\{\{a\},\{b\}\}$: the support and partition coincide, but the union has an empty top stratum. P05 checks the warning and identifies order information as the missing datum.
notes.context: Restates S5 §2 / SA21-R5-07 and provides an elementary analogy to RS PATHS E.10’s warning that marked components alone do not determine mapping spaces; E119/36 retains more than stratum labels.

notes.text: For compatible figures, “même support” does force equality because the common-support formula identifies exactly the common members. Compatibility cannot be dropped, as N010-1 shows; this conditional rigidity is the key input to the maximal-subdivision proof on scan024.
notes.context: Restates S5 §2 / SA21-R5-06 and adds the explicit dependency used later; E119/28–30’s geometric supports alone have no comparable uniqueness claim.

notes.place: comparison prompted by the partition counterexample
notes.text: Use the pair in N010-1 as the first unit test for any proposed functor that sends a figure only to its stratum partition: it must distinguish the two incidence orders or explicitly declare that information forgotten. This is a test of data loss, not a counterexample to the fully coherent exit or normal-link results in RS.
notes.context: Adds a minimal finite test beside E119/58–59 and the warning in RS EXIT_ONE_TYPE P4e; it does not re-prove that geometric result.
notes.confidence: High for the test: the two families and their distinct orders are explicit; no geometric realization claim is made.

notes.text: “admet des Sup majorés” is correct: inside a common upper figure the subfigures are downsets, and their arbitrary union is again a downset. P05 also proves that any pairwise compatible collection has its union as a figure, so the finite-sup detour is unnecessary in this concrete model.
notes.context: Restates S5 §2 and STUDY §2.5’s C1 in its set model; E119/31–32’s stability under geometric gluing is a separate, stronger ambition.

notes.text: The cancelled “un peu vif|cf.” and “il faut passer|préciser par des Sup finis”, together with “explicitons|expliciter … Prop ou Cor”, qualify the exposition locally. They must be retained as tentative or drafting language even though P05 checks C1; C02’s blanket “None explicitly marked” needs this qualification.
notes.context: Adds the marginal drafting instruction to C02’s own caveat and differs from treating S5 §2’s clean theorem summary as the entire manuscript state; E119/34 is a comparison in method, not a proof source.

notes.text: “cas du Sup … vide” correctly singles out the empty family as the least figure. It must be distinguished from the family containing the empty set, which is inadmissible because that member has empty stratum; P00 and the computation both enforce this distinction.
notes.context: Restates the distinction explicitly used in S5 §§1–3 and STUDY’s axioms; E119/27–41 contains no competing empty-family convention.

notes.text: “un ens fermé est irréductible (au sens fort) sss il a un plus grand élément” is correct for complete join-irreducibility. P03 proves it by expressing a downset as the union of its principal downsets, and this qualification repairs the mathematical scope of scan005’s shorter wording.
notes.context: Restates S5 §2 with the strong sense made explicit and qualifies its §1 summary; E119/36’s ordered index set does not settle the distinction.

notes.text: The principal subfigures displayed are $F_X$, but the trailing phrase literally says “pour Y∈…” rather than indexing them by $X$. P05 checks the evident decomposition over $X\in F$; the mismatch is recorded as a reading question and left in the frozen text.
notes.context: Differs from the normalized C2 in S5 §2 and adds a literal indexing caution to STUDY §2.5; E119/36’s Drap(I) is a different indexing construction.

notes.text: C3 and the “Remords” make compatibility testable on principal multistrates and their intersections. The proof in P05 uses the unchanged lower sets from each compatible pair, so it remains valid for infinite families; this is a positive local criterion despite the later failure of C4.
notes.context: Restates S5 §2 / SA21-R5-06 and distinguishes C1–C3 from STUDY §2.5’s extra component axiom; E119/36–37 motivates richer local data without this criterion.

notes.text: The extra braces in the frozen display are not silently flattened into a family of subsets. Even its natural well-typed interpretation $\{A,\{x\},A\cup\{x\}\}$ fails admissibility, since the two lower members cover the top; the proposed comparability bridge therefore fails independently of the brace ambiguity.
notes.context: Confirms the substantive counterexample of SA21-K5-01 / S5 §3 while differing from its cleaned display; E119/40–41 gives no justification for this bridge.

notes.text: For every nonempty ground set, the multistrate $\{L\}$ is isolated: a nonempty lower figure equals it, and any upper figure would violate down-closure unless it also equals it. For $|L|\ge2$ it is incompatible with the distinct node $\{\{x\}\}$, so both connectedness and cross-component compatibility fail even for infinite $L$. P06 gives the complete argument.
notes.context: Strengthens S5 §3’s finite computation to a uniform obstruction; differs from E119/40–41’s contractible-choice requirement rather than solving it.
notes.confidence: High: down-closure at the member L leaves no possible additional member.

notes.text: For finite $n\ge3$, P06 predicts and proves exactly $n+2$ components: $\{L\}$ alone, the two nodes $\{A\}$ and $\{A,L\}$ for each $(n-1)$-subset $A$, and one component of everything else. The valid bridge $\{A,\{x\},A\cup\{x,y\}\}$ uses a second outside point $y$ to keep the top stratum nonempty. Independent exhaustive enumeration verifies the exact partition through $n=4$, not merely its component count.
notes.context: Adds a finite classification to S5 §3 and a precise repair of the failed bridge; E119/40–41 contains no such component calculation.
notes.confidence: High for finite n: written proof plus independent exhaustive checks; no extension of the classification to arbitrary infinite families is claimed.

notes.text: “M est connexe” for finite figures is false as soon as $|L|\ge2$: there are three components on two points and five on three points. P06 and the independent enumeration refute this statement; the manuscript does not withdraw it within scans002–025.
notes.context: Confirms SA21-K5-01 / SA21-R5-08 and contradicts the manuscript claim, without promoting S to a visual witness; E119/40–41 asks for an even stronger form of choice-independence.

notes.text: C4 is false in this model, not merely unsupported by the connectedness argument. On two points the figures $\{\{a\},\{a,b\}\}$ and $\{\{b\},\{a,b\}\}$ lie in different components and have inadmissible union; P06 also gives the universal isolated-node counterexample.
notes.context: Confirms S5 §3 and STUDY §2.5’s stated obstruction to the fourth system; the later absence of a component axiom in the sweep’s account of 156-6 does not establish why it was dropped.

notes.text: Even a repaired connectedness theorem would control only components, whereas the “choix anodins” principle in the context asks for contractible spaces of choices and retains higher homotopy. Thus this page’s proposed connectedness argument cannot alone justify an invariant construction up to coherent choice.
notes.context: Differs in strength from E119/40–41 and bears on the scope of RS EXIT_ONE_TYPE P1d1 and MPL_150_044-084 N35.

notes.text: The claim “M=∅, et M est connexe” uses a convention allowing the empty space to be connected, while the singleton case is explicitly “0-connexe”. The finite counterexamples begin at two points and do not depend on this convention; nonemptiness would still have to be specified for any space-of-choices application.
notes.context: Adds a convention warning to S5 §3 and differs from the nonempty contractible choice spaces envisaged in E119/40–41.

notes.place: literal ranges in the boxtimes formula
notes.text: With the literal ranges $A\in F$, $B\in G$, the extra condition “pas tous deux ∅” is redundant because admissible families contain no empty-set member. For singleton factors the displayed product is $\{\{a,b\}\}$ and is admissible, but contains neither factor as a subfigure, contrary to the later claim; P07 separates these two assertions.
notes.context: Qualifies S5 §3’s blanket assertion of inadmissibility, while retaining its refutation of the bounding argument; E119/28–30’s geometric gluing does not fix the displayed ranges.

notes.place: intended inclusion of the disjoint union of factors
notes.text: If empty choices are adjoined to both factors so that the product contains $F\amalg G$, every mixed member $A\cup B$ has the proper lower members $A$ and $B$ covering it. Its open stratum is then empty, so this enlarged construction cannot be the asserted multistrate or rescue connectedness.
notes.context: Confirms the intended-construction objection in SA21-K5-01 / S5 §3, with the extra interpretation stated rather than inserted into the transcription; E119/36 requires genuine additional geometric pieces.

notes.text: The printed boundary identity already fails for the literal singleton-factor product, whose actual boundary is empty. The stratum identity fails for $F=\{\{a\},\{a,a'\}\}$ and $G=\{\{b\}\}$: the product’s top stratum is $\{a'\}$, not $\{a',b\}$. P07 refutes the identities separately from the ambiguity about empty choices.
notes.context: Adds a literal-range counterexample to S5 §3 and explains why its argument and the ink need separate formulations; no corresponding identity is supplied by E119/27–41.

notes.text: “les supports correspondent aux parties quelconques” is correct in the full set-theoretic figure model. P08 proves orthogonality by disjoint supports and uses point figures to identify the double orthogonal with all figures supported on the union, yielding exactly $\mathcal P(L)$.
notes.context: Restates S5 §4 / SA21-R5-09 and the concrete model in STUDY §2.5; E119/28–30 supplies a geometric closed/complement pair but no abstract support-lattice theorem.

notes.place: scope of the Boolean support lattice
notes.text: The computation of $\mathcal P(L)$ proves Booleanity for this model only. It cannot be transferred to every abstract biorthogonal-support system in the sweep, where STUDY records non-distributive examples from156-7; those outside scans are background here, not newly checked examples.
notes.context: Differs in generality from STUDY’s abstract systems and prevents treating S5 §4 as a universal theorem; E119/31–34 explicitly allows a range of tame settings.

notes.place: comparison with support formalism in RS
notes.text: The set complement behind “cosupports” supplies the simplest closed/open separation, but no coefficient category or adjunction has been constructed. Therefore this is an illustration alongside the registered recollement formalism, not an independent proof of it.
notes.context: Adds an elementary model beside E119/38 and RS BISITE F.9 / STRATA D.2; the registered derivator claims are carried as background only.

notes.text: The parenthesis “L se récupère … points isolés” is mathematically significant: $L$ is already recovered as the atoms of $\mathcal P(L)$, and these correspond to isolated principal ultrafilters in its Stone space. P08 checks the atom identification; it does not claim that a passage to Stone space irretrievably loses the original point set.
notes.context: Restates the parenthetical correction in S5 §4 and adds the direct atom description; E119/33–34 discusses category comparison, not this Stone reconstruction.

notes.text: “Ceci suggère de refaire” the theory on a compact discontinuous space is a proposed change of setting, not a completed equivalence of theories. Under explicit zero-dimensional Hausdorff hypotheses and clopen supports, P08 derives regular open sets as the biorthogonally closed supports, using $U^*=\operatorname{int}(X\setminus U)$ and $U^{**}=\operatorname{int}\overline U$.
notes.context: Adds a topological variant to S5 §4 and differs from E119/31–34’s broader comparison of moderate theories; it does not settle RS MPL_150_044-084 Q9.

notes.text: The frozen final line has `\overline U\unsure{\geq|=}\operatorname{int}(\overline U)`, while the intended fixed-point relation suggested by the orthogonality calculation is $U=\operatorname{int}\overline U$. The preceding formula for $V$ also repeats a symbol read as “f U”; P08 states the coherent complementary pair $V=X\setminus\overline U$, $U=X\setminus\overline V$ without substituting it into the ink.
notes.context: Differs from S5 §4’s clean regular-open summary; E119/31–34 offers no deciding reading for these rewritten formulas.

notes.place: NB, figures as closed compatible sets of multistrates
notes.text: The NB reconstructs a figure from all its principal multistrates as a down-closed, pairwise compatible subset of $M$. P05’s arbitrary-compatible-union argument proves the converse: form the union, and every principal multistrate of that union already lies in the original down-closed set. Thus this reconstruction survives the failure of connectedness.
notes.context: Adds an explicit proof to the NB and restates the set-model interpretation in S5 §§2–4; E119/58–59’s internal-category reconstruction still retains additional geometric data.

notes.text: “Toute condition portant sur la nature des strates … ou … multistrates” is stable under subfigures and compatible unions because the member and its entire lower subfamily remain unchanged. P09 checks this local stability statement; a condition on the whole collection, such as local finiteness, needs the separate qualification on scan019.
notes.context: Restates S5 §4 and adds the mechanism underlying the assertion; E119/31–32’s desired stability axioms are more geometric than this set-level argument.

notes.text: For closed members, “A=closure(A°)” is equivalent to the stated incidence condition $A\subseteq B\Rightarrow A^\circ\subseteq\overline{B^\circ}$: one direction uses $A^\circ\subset A\subset B$, and the other sums the lower strata of $B$. P09 spells out where closedness is needed; the assertion is not taken as a theorem for arbitrary subsets of an arbitrary topological space.
notes.context: Adds a hypothesis-aware proof to S5 §4’s list; E119/36–39 discusses stratified structures with extra data, not this bare density test.

notes.text: The cancelled “peut-être” and “saurait-il” introduce a tentative relaxation involving “préadmissibles”, but intervening words remain uncertain. The precise proposed axiom cannot responsibly be reconstructed from the mathematics or the context; this is a retained self-flagged fragment, not a newly formulated conjecture.
notes.context: Restates C03’s caution; E119/34’s provisional axioms and RS MPL_150_044-084 Q9 are thematic parallels only, not evidence for missing words.

notes.text: Conditions such as “i-connexe” or boundaries being “sphères topologiques” restrict individual pieces, but do not by themselves specify the linking maps or meridian injections needed for an ordinary exit category. These pages therefore do not overturn the register’s warning that aspherical strata alone are insufficient.
notes.context: Differs in data from E119/35–36 and119/58–59; bears on RS STRATA F.3, EXIT_ONE_TYPE P1a1 / P1b1, and MPL_150_044-084 N39.

notes.text: “pas … généralement par sup quelconque” is witnessed by the singleton figures at $1/n$ in $\mathbb R$: each is locally finite, but their compatible union is not locally finite at zero. Finite unions of locally finite collections remain locally finite, so P09 verifies both sides of the distinction.
notes.context: Restates S5 §4’s qualification and supplies an explicit example; E119/39’s finite stratifying filtrations do not justify arbitrary unions.

notes.text: “de t. f. et ses strates sont finies” must refer to finiteness of the principal multistrates if it is to characterize a finite figure. Cardinality of the subsets themselves cannot be intended mathematically: the one-member family $\{L\}$ is finite even when $L$ is infinite. P09 checks the principal-subfamily interpretation and leaves the literal wording intact.
notes.context: Adds a terminology qualification to S5 §4; E119/36 uses geometric strata rather than the principal-family finiteness meant here.

notes.text: For a finite poset $I$, take $X=|NI|$ and $X_i=|N(\downarrow i)|$; the maximal vertex with positive barycentric coordinate identifies the nonempty strata and gives the required admissible family. P10 proves the closed-downset correspondence directly and records the order reversal needed before comparing it with the register’s minimum-vertex convention.
notes.context: Adds a specific construction to this page and E119/36; RS STRATA A.4, STRATA A.12, and BISITE G.10 remain background for the stronger exit statements.
notes.confidence: High for finite posets: the simplicial construction is explicit; no unrestricted geometric or exit theorem is inferred.

notes.text: The construction in N019-3 does not make every closed piece a regular closed ball: three incomparable points below a greatest point give a tripod. Thus the written “cellules” must not silently be strengthened to regular CW cells, and the sphere-boundary restrictions from scan018 remain additional requirements.
notes.context: Differs in strength from a regular-cell reading, and separates this page from E119/35’s tubular questions and the registered realization comparisons.

notes.text: “qui sera développée” explicitly postpones the subdivision terminology, then the same page begins its definition through refinement. The common cell covering provides a finer figure on the relevant support, but the word does not yet assert a geometric subdivision theorem up to isotopy.
notes.context: Adds an explicit algebraic refinement notion to E119/33–34’s triangulation programme; RS MPL_150_044-084 Q2 and Q9 remain unsolved by this terminology.

notes.text: “un plus petit élément phi(A)” is a least container in the second figure; its existence is stronger than choosing a minimal container. Together with closed intersections it is equivalent to a monotone map on stratum quotients, as P11 proves on scans020–023.
notes.context: Restates S5 §5 / SA21-R5-10 and gives a concrete underlying map for the order language of E119/36–37 and RS WG2 B15 (§1.2).

notes.text: These pages provide finite figures, refinement, and subdivision, which are ingredients for the proposed S14 system of finite cuttings. They do not define a form, network, cutting, or workshop, construct a pro-object, prove cofilteredness of all chosen cuttings, or prove recovery of a tame space from such a system. The planning guess is therefore supported only at the level of vocabulary and elementary models, not confirmed as a theorem.
notes.context: Adds ingredients to MPL_156-5/README.md’s S14 and differs from its reconstruction expectation; E119/36 and119/58–59 explicitly retain attachment data.

notes.text: The literal top line has “A∩F” where the continuation repeatedly uses $A\cap B$. P11 checks the latter well-typed formulation, which is also what S5 summarizes; the frozen transcription is not silently repaired.
notes.context: Differs from S5 §5’s normalized condition a; E119/36’s index diagrams do not decide this local symbol.

notes.place: a implies b and marginal lemma
notes.text: The marginal lemma “A°⊂B alors A⊂B” under b is the key to both directions. P11 proves it by decomposing $A$ into lower strata and using monotonicity of their assigned containers, then verifies that the resulting container is least.
notes.context: Restates S5 §5 / SA21-R5-10 with the logical dependency isolated; E119/36 gives no substitute for this proof.

notes.place: NB, continuity of the support inclusion
notes.text: The NB correctly identifies the closed-intersection condition, together with support inclusion, with continuity for the two preorder topologies. P11 checks that continuity forces every $F$-stratum into a unique $G$-stratum and makes the induced quotient map increasing, so no independent least-container choice is needed.

notes.text: The inverse-image claim follows from $qi=\varphi p$ if “modérée” means saturated, and also under the finite-figure convention of scan006. If instead it means the ordinary Boolean algebra generated by a possibly infinite figure, it can fail: singleton strata on $\mathbb N$ refine the even/odd two-piece figure, but the inverse image of the even piece is not finite–cofinite. P13 therefore checks the stated meaning explicitly rather than extending scan006’s finite assertion.
